new_statements.quote: Tsiapera (1969: 16) provides the following rules of stress placement in CyA: 1) all long vowels carry stress 2) the final syllable of words ending in VCC carries stress as in: raxímt 'I blessed.' mindàxt 'downstairs' 3) Primary stress on the antepenult is infrequent but unpredictable, as in: núṣuxar 'noon' [...] kúzubra 'coriander' 4) primary stress most commonly falls on the penult as in: yabàtak 'your (masc.) father.' In words consisting of a verbal nucleus, the stress is placed on the first syllable "even when heavy syllables intervene closer to the final word boundary" as in the following examples (from Borg, 2006: 540): ʕížipna 'we liked it.' tàxakilla 'he cheated her.' šàttimna 'he abused us.'
new_statements.citation: Shormani, Mohammed Q. 2023. Cypriot Arabic: Language contact and linguistic deviations from Mainstream Arabic norms. new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK. Opened (22 pp.) with extracted text. Section '3.3. Stress in CyA' is present and every phrase of the reported quote is there word for word (15 exact-string checks against the extracted text all matched, including the diacritics raxímt / mindàxt / núṣuxar / kúzubra / yabàtak / ʕížipna / tàxakilla / šàttimna and the Borg 2006: 540 attribution; the reader's '[...]' stands for the parenthetical '(literally: half of a day')'). The only discrepancy is the locator: the section begins on PDF p. 10 and runs onto PDF p. 11, i.e. journal pp. 43-44 by the running footers ('Page | 43' closes the page on which 3.3 starts; the stress-group and kull examples are on 'Page | 44'), not 'pp. 42-43…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Two second-hand reports do not reduce to one rule. Tsiapera 1969 (as reported): stress is weight-sensitive — a long vowel attracts stress, a final superheavy (VCC) syllable is stressed, otherwise the penult is the default, with antepenult stress rare and unpredictable. Borg 2006 (as reported): in words built on a verbal nucleus (inflected verbs, numeral+pronoun compounds) stress is on the FIRST syllable regardless of heavy syllables later in the word (ʕížipna, síttiṭkon, xàlluon 'leave them!' vs xallùon 'they left them'), a pattern Borg compares to Neo-Aramaic; in stress groups (kull + noun) the first word carries the group stress (kùyyom 'every day'). Armostis & Karyolemou 2023 independently note antepenult-stressed compounds (/ˈkullajle/, /ˈnuṣṣullajl/). If forced to one label for simple (nominal) words, Tsiapera's rules read as weight-sensitive with penult default.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenult stress 'infrequent but unpredictable' (Tsiapera); a minimal pair by stress xàlluon 'leave them!' vs xallùon 'they left them' (Borg 2006 via Shormani); stress groups where 'the second word loses its stress' (Borg 2006 quoting Jastrow 1997: 353 on Neo-Aramaic as the parallel).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (isolated citation forms and inflected verbs); Borg also describes phrase-level stress groups (kull + noun) with a single stress on the first word. The stress diacritics in Shormani's transcription are inconsistent (grave and acute both used for primary stress).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the single surviving variety, the Arabic of Kormakiti/Kormakitis village (Kyrenia district), now spoken mainly in Nicosia; community name Sanna. No dialect split; glottocode cypr1248 applies as is.

sources.note: Section 3.3 'Stress in CyA' (pp. 42-43) reports second-hand: Tsiapera (1969: 16) — long vowels carry stress; final syllable of words ending in VCC stressed; antepenult stress infrequent and unpredictable; primary stress most commonly on the penult; and Borg (2006: 540) — words with a verbal nucleus stress the first syllable even when heavy syllables intervene closer to the final boundary (ʕížipna, tàxakilla, šàttimna, tlàxitna, síttiṭkon, xàlluon vs xallùon), a Neo-Aramaic-like pattern; stress groups (kùyyom 'every day').
